items.text: Partially drain the pool and refill it with fresh water.

notes.text: If you drain, refill straight away and skip the other steps, unless there's algae: treat that first.
Don't drain if the water table is high.

items.text: With the pump running, spread alkalinity increaser over the water: **6 lb 13 oz** in total, never more than **9 lb** at once.
Retest after adding half.
If you add it in more than one dose, wait **4 hours** between doses.
Wait **4 hours** after the last dose.

notes.text: Don't add it on the same day as calcium increaser.

items.text: With the pump running, pour **50 lb 10 oz** of pool salt slowly around the pool edge.
Brush the pool floor.

notes.text: Don't add salt if the water is below **60 °F**.

weekly.note: Set the generator to hold this
Only with heavy use, animals or debris

overall: Stabiliser (CYA) read **5** on both tests. Without stabiliser, sunlight burns off chlorine within a few hours, which likely explains free chlorine falling from **2.33** to **0.25**. Step 5 matters more than its position suggests.
pH rose from **6.9** to **8.7** in five days. Salt-chlorine pools tend to push pH up, so check pH more often than weekly for a while.

3: Acid lowers alkalinity as well as pH. Finish step 2 and retest before adding acid.

overall: Stabiliser (CYA) has read **5**, **5** and now **6** across three tests, so it has not been added yet. It is still the main reason chlorine is hard to hold steady; step 6 matters more than its position suggests.
Free chlorine is **13.8** (Nov 9: **15**), well above the **1–4** range for a second test. That points to the salt generator output being set high; the store's step 4 tip says to turn it down.

Salt went **2524** → **2889** → **2284** and calcium **671** → **603** → **649** over three tests. Swings this size without matching drains or additions suggest test variation; worth asking the store to retest salt before adding the full **68 lb 9 oz**.

5: Combined chlorine is **1.18** (total **14.98** minus free **13.8**). Oxidising shock can itself show up as combined chlorine on some tests for a day, which is why the store says to wait **24 hours** before retesting.
3: Acid lowers alkalinity as well as pH. Finish step 2 and retest before adding acid.
